summary: Kiribati waives visas for citizens of around 120 countries and territories listed in its 2023 visa exemption order — including the UK, Ireland, most of the EU, the US, China, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and its Pacific neighbors — who may stay up to 90 days in any 12 months. Everyone else must obtain a visitor visa from Kiribati Immigration before traveling. All visitors need a passport valid six months, an onward ticket and funds for the stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration — visitor visas

passportValidity.text: Carry a passport valid for at least 6 months beyond your intended departure from Kiribati. Airlines serving Tarawa apply the rule strictly, and there is no way to fix a validity problem once you are on the atoll.

source.name: Kiribati — Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023
source.instrument: Immigration Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023, made under s.62 of the Immigration Act 2019 (in force 1 September 2023), para. 3.3

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not an entry condition and is not checked on arrival. It matters more here than in most places: Tungaru Central Hospital on South Tarawa covers basic care only, and anything serious means a medical evacuation to Fiji, Australia or New Zealand on a flight that may not leave for days. Make sure your policy explicitly covers evacuation from a remote Pacific island.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration — entry requirements

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed onward or return ticket is required, along with the name of where you are staying. With only a handful of flights a week, immigration officers expect the ticket to match a realistic departure date.

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors are expected to show they can support themselves for the stay. No figure is published; because cards are barely usable in Kiribati, bringing Australian dollars in cash is the practical way to satisfy this.

declarations.name: Arrival Card, Customs and Quarantine Declaration
declarations.text: Passengers complete a paper arrival card with customs and quarantine declarations, distributed on the flight. Food, plant material and animal products are controlled to protect a fragile atoll environment. Declare anything of the sort.

source.name: Kiribati Immigration Procedures 2020 — passenger responsibilities on arrival

notes: Kiribati is an atoll nation with strict quarantine rules: fresh food, seeds, plants and soil-covered equipment must be declared and may be refused entry.
Alcohol imports are limited and licensing is restricted on some islands. Check local rules before bringing bottles as gifts.

The Phoenix Islands Protected Area and several outer islands need permission from the relevant ministry before you may visit or land; arrange it well in advance through the Immigration Division or your tour operator.

payments.text: Kiribati runs on cash. Card acceptance is close to non-existent outside one or two hotels on South Tarawa, ATMs are few and can be empty or offline, and there is no reliable way to draw money on the outer islands. Bring enough Australian dollars in cash for the whole trip, in small denominations.

safety.text: Crime against visitors is rare and Kiribati is a calm, friendly place. The real hazards are practical: very limited medical care, thin transport links, contaminated water and, on densely populated South Tarawa, poor sanitation. King tides and coastal flooding affect low-lying areas several times a year.

source.name: UK FCDO — Kiribati: safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the drier, slightly less humid half of the year on Tarawa and the best window for bonefishing and diving. Kiribati sits on the equator outside the main cyclone belt, so heat and rainfall — not storms — decide the season.

tips.text: Treat Kiribati as a cash-only country. Bring Australian dollars for the entire stay including the departure taxes and any boat charter. A card that fails on South Tarawa cannot be rescued, and there is no banking at all on most outer islands.

Medical facilities are very limited. Tungaru Central Hospital handles basic emergencies; anything beyond that requires evacuation to Fiji or Australia, which depends on flight availability. Carry a full personal medical kit and any prescription drugs you need, plus a copy of the prescription.

Tarawa is served by only a few international flights a week, mainly from Nadi and Brisbane via Nauru, and cancellations cascade. Leave two or three buffer days before any onward international connection, and never book a same-day connection out of Fiji.

Kiribati spans three time zones across 3,000 km — Tarawa and the Gilberts are UTC+12, the Phoenix Islands UTC+13 and the Line Islands, including Kiritimati, UTC+14, the earliest time zone on earth. Check which group your flight lands in before you calculate a connection.

Do not drink tap or well water. Use bottled, boiled or treated water, including for brushing teeth. Equatorial sun on a treeless atoll is fierce even on cloudy days, so plan for shade, high-factor sunscreen and far more water than you think you need.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kiribati?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Kiribati's Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023 waives the visa for citizens of around 120 countries and territories, including the UK, Ireland, most EU states, the US, Canada, China, Japan, Australia, New Zealand and Kiribati's Pacific neighbors; they may stay up to 90 days in any 12 months. Everyone else must obtain a visitor visa before traveling. A traveler who arrives with neither a visa nor an exemption is liable to be turned around.

faq.question: How do I get a visitor visa if my country is not exempt?
faq.answer: Apply before you travel, on Kiribati Immigration's visitor visa application form (published on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration website), and email visaofficer@mfa.gov.ki for payment details. You will need evidence of funds for the stay and of onward travel. Kiribati has very few overseas missions, so allow plenty of time before your flight.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Kiribati?
faq.answer: Kiribati's 2023 exemption order allows visa-exempt visitors up to 90 days in any 12-month period. UK travel advice says one month is normally granted on arrival and extended a month at a time by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration in Bairiki, Tarawa; the order's 90 days is the legal limit. Apply before your current permission expires, since there is no other office to turn to.

faq.question: Can I visit the outer islands and Kiritimati freely?
faq.answer: Your entry permission covers the country, but travel to the outer islands is limited by transport rather than paperwork, and the Phoenix Islands Protected Area needs a permit from the responsible ministry. Kiritimati (Christmas Island) in the Line Islands has its own international flights and its own time zone. Plan it as a separate leg from Tarawa, not a day trip.

faq.question: Is travel insurance required for Kiribati?
faq.answer: No, it is not an entry requirement and nobody will ask for it. It is still strongly advisable, and specifically insurance that covers medical evacuation from a remote island — local care is basic and getting out requires a chartered or scheduled flight that may be days away.

faq.question: Can I use cards or ATMs in Kiribati?
faq.answer: Barely. A couple of hotels on South Tarawa take cards, ATMs are scarce and unreliable, and the outer islands have no banking. Kiribati uses the Australian dollar, so bring cash in AUD and budget for the whole trip in advance.
